findings.issue: The Crop task bar's Generative Expand panics on any document wider or taller than 30,000 px. `(w + left + right).round().clamp(w, 30_000.0)` calls f64::clamp with min = the document's width, and f64::clamp always asserts min <= max, including in release builds. When w > 30,000 the assert fails whatever the frame is. Nothing in the UI draw path catches the panic. Documents up to 300,000 px a side are legal (file.new 1..300000, and ai.generativeExpand's own side() limit is 300,000).
findings.scenario: Connect an OpenAI or Gemini key, so the item shows (fits(Image)). Open or create a 32,000 x 2,000 px panorama. Press C for the Crop tool (the contextual task bar is on by default). Click 'Generative Expand' in the bar. Result: panic 'min > max, or either was NaN. min = 32000.0, max = 30000.0', the app goes down, and unsaved work is lost. Even below the crash, the window's 'New width' DragValue is capped at 30,000 while the engine accepts 300,000.
findings.test: tests/it/ai.rs: a harness with with_mock (an image key), app.run("file.new", {"width":30001,"height":200}), app.ui.tool = Tool::Crop, app.ui.crop_rect = Some([0.0,0.0,30001.0,200.0]). Call ai_ui::task_bar::expand_from_crop(app). Today it panics. With the fix: generate.open is true, generate.width == 30001, generate.height == 200, anchor 'center'. A second case drags the frame 100 px past the right edge and expects width 30101, anchor 'left'.
findings.fix: Never call clamp with a bound taken from input. Use `(w + left + right).round().max(w).min(300_000.0)` (and the same for h), with the engine's limit as a shared constant. In generate.rs:448/450 use `.range(w0..=300_000)` (and h0).

findings.where: crates/ui-egui/src/ai_ui/accounts.rs:563-565 (the synthetic-input filter) with 827-847 (model fields and Use Suggested/Automatic edit the Form directly) and 167-171, 500-508 (close() and switch() call save_models); crates/ui-egui/src/ai_ui/generate.rs:520-522 and 224-236 (start saves image_provider and the last prompt before app.run's gate refusal)
findings.issue: Review45 made AI Accounts drop every act of synthetic input except Switch and Close. The Chat model and Image model fields, and the 'Use Suggested' and 'Automatic' buttons, write into Form.chat_model and Form.image_model while drawing, not through an act. Close and Switch, which synthetic input may still trigger, then call save_models and write those values to ai.json. So an agent without 'Allow agents to run AI commands' can choose which models the person's own later requests are billed on. Review45 fixed the same thing in the Assistant window (#4). The Generate window has the same hole: an agent's click on a Provider label sets app.ai.generate.provider directly, and its click on Generate runs start(), which saves settings.image_provider (and the last prompt) before app.run is refused by gate.
findings.scenario: 'Allow agents to run AI commands' is off. An agent sends engine.execute ai.accounts (allowed, it sends nothing). It sends ui.click on the Image model field, ui.type 'gpt-image-1' (or clicks 'Use Suggested'), then ui.click on Done. ai.json now holds openai.imageModel = gpt-image-1, and the person's next Generative Fill is billed on that model. In the same way, with two providers connected: an agent opens Edit > Generative Fill…, clicks 'Google Gemini', then clicks Generate. The request is refused, but imageProvider is now gemini, so the next request goes to (and is billed by) the other account.
findings.test: tests/it/ai.rs, beside synthetic_input_neither_sends_nor_grants_itself_permission: open AI Accounts. Synthetic-click the 'Image model' field, then push egui::Event::Text("gpt-image-1") in a synthetic batch (as ui.type does), or synthetic_click 'Use Suggested' after a cached catalog. Then synthetic_click 'Done'. Assert with_accounts(settings.models(OpenAi).image_model) is unchanged (today it is Some("gpt-image-1")). For the Generate window: two providers connected, synthetic_click the second provider and 'Generate', then assert settings.image_provider is unchanged.
findings.fix: In accounts::show, when app.automation_input && !agents_allowed(app), reload f.chat_model and f.image_model from the saved settings after body() (load_models), so typed or suggested values never reach save_models. Do the same for f.timeout. Alternatively, make save_models refuse while automation_input. In generate::start, run super::gate(app, feature, &params)? before with_accounts(...save...), and ignore Provider clicks from synthetic input without the permission, as assistant::show does.

findings.issue: 'Generative Expand' shows in the Crop bar whenever a provider has an image key (fits(Image)), even when ai.generativeExpand is disabled for the document: layered_doc refuses Bitmap, Indexed, Duotone and Multichannel. expand_from_crop first calls crop_ui::dismiss, which throws away the person's crop frame. Only then does it call generate::open, and when open fails it returns without a word (the Err is dropped and nothing goes to the status bar or a notice).
findings.scenario: Image key connected. Open an Indexed Color GIF and choose the Crop tool. Drag the frame past the canvas (or set a ratio and a straighten angle). Click 'Generative Expand'. The frame disappears and nothing else happens: no window, no message. The person's frame setup is lost.
findings.test: tests/it/ai.rs: file.new, then image.mode.indexedColor (or any mode layered() refuses), Tool::Crop, crop_rect Some(frame). Call expand_from_crop. Assert crop_rect is still Some(frame) and app.ui.status (or the item's disabled tooltip) carries 'Generative AI needs an RGB, CMYK, Lab or Grayscale document'. Today crop_rect is None and the status is empty.
findings.fix: In crop_item, add the button with add_enabled(app.session.disabled_reason(EXPAND).is_none(), …) and put the reason in on_disabled_hover_text. In expand_from_crop, call generate::open before crop_ui::dismiss, and write the Err to app.ui.status (status_error = true) when it fails.

findings.issue: When a Remove Background job ends, removed_background records app.session.active() as the document 'as Remove Background left it'. That is whichever tab is active when the event arrives, not the job's document (e.document). The task bar then offers 'Generate Background…' on a document that never had its background removed, and not on the one that did.
findings.scenario: Doc A: Layer > Remove Background with AI Provider (a background job, several seconds; A is locked). Meanwhile, click tab B. The job lands on A. Result: after_remove = (B, B.revision), so B shows the 'Generate Background…' bar (when B has no selection) and A does not. Clicking it opens Generate Background for B's active layer, which still has its background.
findings.test: tests/it/ai.rs: two documents and a MockBackend with background jobs. Run ai.removeBackground {"method":"provider"} on A, set_active(B) before until_idle, then until_idle. Assert app.ai.after_remove == Some((A.id, A.revision)), task_bar::which(app) == None on B, and Some(Bar::AfterRemove) after switching back to A.
findings.fix: Pass the event's document: removed_background(app, e.document). Look that document up in app.session.documents() and take its revision; in remove_background(), keep the active document for the inline (non-job) case.

findings.issue: The Assistant's 'List models' link shows only while lists has no entry for the provider. Once a list fails (a network error, a 401, a timeout, or the person pressing Cancel on the status bar's 'ai.testConnection' job), the entry is ModelList::Failed for the rest of the session. That arm draws only the error, so the person can never ask again. Nothing clears lists: not set_provider, not known_models, not a new key in AI Accounts.
findings.scenario: Open Window > Assistant with no cached catalog. Click 'List models' while offline (or cancel it in the status bar). It shows 'Could not list models: …'. Go back online. There is no 'List models' link any more, and the Chat model menu offers only Automatic and the saved model until Pigment restarts. Connecting a different key in AI Accounts does not refresh it either.
findings.test: tests/it/ai_assistant.rs: a Recorder whose list_models fails once and then answers two chat models. Call assistant::list_models, then until_idle. Assert listed_models(OpenAi) is None and h.query_by_label("List models") is Some (today it is None). Click it, until_idle, and assert the two models are listed.
findings.fix: In the Failed arm, also draw a 'Try again' link (Act::ListModels). Better, let list_models replace any non-Loading entry and show the link for both None and Failed. Remove the provider's entry when AI Accounts connects, removes a key or signs out (reread).

findings.issue: Every frame, for every step of every message in the active document's conversation, assistant_row does two costly things. (1) It serializes the call's whole arguments (`c.args.to_string()`) to build a hover text it then cuts to 400 characters, even when nothing is hovered. (2) describe_call clones the arguments (parse_maybe_json) and, for apply_*, runs find_kind, which allocates a lower-cased String for every registry spec, twice. Review45 bounded one step to 64 KiB of arguments, but one answer may hold 32 steps and a turn 12 rounds. So one message can hold about 24 MiB of arguments, and a 40-message conversation several hundred MiB. That much is held in memory and re-serialized every frame (every 100 ms during a turn, and on every pointer move after).
findings.scenario: A provider (or a model in a loop) answers each of 12 rounds with 32 add_text calls whose arguments are about 60 KiB each (allowed: under ARGS_LIMIT, and add_text keeps 2,000 characters). The Assistant window then serializes about 23 MB of JSON per frame for that one message, and the interface stutters or freezes while the window is open. A few such turns multiply it, and memory grows by the same amount.
findings.test: Unit test in assistant.rs (or tests/it/ai_assistant.rs): after a turn whose answer has calls with 60,000-character arguments, assert that what a Call keeps for display is bounded, e.g. a `detail: String` of at most 400 characters and a `label: String`. Either assert that Call.args is not retained beyond a preview, or time one frame of the window with 32 x 12 such calls and assert it is under 50 ms.
findings.fix: When a step is pushed (run_call), compute the label (describe_call) and a 400-character detail once and store them on Call. Keep no full args clone for display: the full arguments live in turn.history only. Build the hover text inside on_hover_ui so nothing is formatted unless the pointer is on it.

findings.where: crates/ui-egui/src/ai_ui/accounts.rs:167-171 (close) with 466-480 (save_models) and genai accounts.rs:277-295 (set_models validates both before setting either)
findings.issue: Done (and Esc) calls save_models and then drops the dialog. When the typed Chat model is not a valid model id (check_model_id: a space, a character outside [A-Za-z0-9-._:/], more than 128 bytes), set_models fails before setting either field, so a valid Image model typed in the same visit is lost too. The error is written into the Form that close() is about to drop, so the person never sees it. The lost_focus SaveModels on the press frame shows it for one frame at most.
findings.scenario: In AI Accounts > OpenAI, type 'gpt 5.5' (a space) as Chat model and 'gpt-image-1.5' as Image model, then click Done. The dialog closes. Neither model is saved and nothing says so. The next request runs on the automatic models.
findings.test: tests/it/ai.rs: open AI Accounts, type_into 'Chat model' 'gpt 5.5' and 'Image model' 'gpt-image-1.5', click Done. Today: is_open false and models(OpenAi) == (None, None). Expected: the dialog stays open with the error '`gpt 5.5` is not a model id.' (or the valid image model is saved and the chat error shown).
findings.fix: In close(), run save_models first and keep the dialog open (return) when it noted an error. Make save_models report which field failed, and call set_models per field (Some(chat), None) then (None, Some(image)) so a valid field is kept.

findings.issue: The Assistant's policy blocks app-wide settings and what Undo cannot restore: history.options was blocked as 'an app-wide setting', and the preset libraries may be added to but not changed. Two persisted, app-wide stores are still open to run_command, and Undo restores neither. edit.checkSpelling with action addToDictionary or removeFromDictionary edits prefs.user_dictionary (type_spell_cmds.rs:177-192), and type.font.favorite rewrites prefs.type_.favorite_fonts (font_library_cmds.rs:55-74). Both are engine commands outside every blocked family.
findings.scenario: Text in the attached image or a pasted layer steers the model to call run_command {"id":"edit.checkSpelling","params":{"action":"removeFromDictionary","word":"<a word the person added>"}}, repeatedly, or type.font.favorite {"family":…,"on":false} for each favourite. The person's dictionary and font favourites change for good. Edit > Undo does nothing, and the change survives a restart.
findings.test: Unit test in assistant_tools.rs: blocked("edit.checkSpelling", {"action":"addToDictionary","word":"x"}) and blocked("type.font.favorite", {"family":"Arial"}) are Err. blocked("edit.checkSpelling", {}) and {"action":"list"} stay Ok. In tests/it/ai_assistant.rs: run_command addToDictionary, then assert the step failed and session.prefs().user_dictionary is unchanged.
findings.fix: Add "type.font.favorite" to BLOCKED_IDS. In blocked(), refuse edit.checkSpelling when params.action is addToDictionary, removeFromDictionary or add (the alias add_word accepts). Extend the unit test that asserts each listed id exists.
